primitives.verbatim_quote: It is appended AFTER the existing 0.58 fair-prob floor (moneyline) and after the 0.55 vote / 50 confidence gates (totals), and it returns null whenever `independentEdge == null`.
primitives.assumptions: Edge is computed from market-anchored probabilities; null implies insufficient signal.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When independentEdge is null, fallback to 0.58 fair-prob floor.

primitives.name: Market-Relative Edge Test
primitives.verbatim_quote: Replace the 0.55 over/under vote gate with the same positive-edge test when a market-anchored `p` for the chosen side exists; when it does not, keep the current vote gate unchanged.
primitives.assumptions: Positive edge implies market-relative advantage; vote gate used when no p available.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When p is absent, revert to vote gate behavior.

layer2.mapping: GSI tests edge sign; GSE evaluates conditional gate logic.
layer2.telemetry: Total publish status depends on edge sign or vote gate.

primitives.name: Fallback Null Edge Behavior
primitives.verbatim_quote: When no `p` exists, fall back to the CURRENT behavior (the 0.58 floor), do not return null.
primitives.assumptions: Null edge implies no reliable market signal; fallback ensures minimal publishing.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Null edge triggers 0.58 floor instead of suppression.

layer2.mapping: GSI enforces fallback; GSE ensures consistency in state transition.
layer2.telemetry: Behavioral consistency under null edge condition.

The core operator is a probabilistic edge test that gates publication of predictions. For moneylines, a 0.58 fair-prob floor acts as baseline; for totals, a 0.55 vote gate is applied. When market-anchored probabilities (p) exist, the edge (p - q) determines whether to publish. If p is absent, the system falls back to the vote gate or 0.58 floor. This introduces a dual regime: one where edge-based logic prevails, and another where legacy voting or floor logic applies. The failure mode occurs when edge computation fails (nullEdge), leading to inconsistent fallback behavior unless explicitly constrained. The system thus operates under a hybrid Bayesian-conformal inference framework where edge validity determines publishability, and null-edge cases are resolved through deterministic fallbacks.
